models_evaluated: gradient-boosting machine learning model with similarity cascade and customized loss function

links.outcome: Scheduler case-length prediction accuracy with versus without model assistance in live deployment
links.effect: Model-assisted schedulers predicted 3.4% more cases within 20% of actual length and 4.3% fewer underpredicted cases; the model alone did better still (5.9% more within 20%, 11.2% fewer underpredicted) than schedulers alone.
links.quote: The model assisted schedulers to predict 3.4% more cases within 20% of the actual case length and 4.3% fewer underpredicted cases.

unlisted_practices: custom loss function to balance over- and under-prediction of case length
automated production pipeline for deploying the model across the institution

screen.reason: The study prospective evaluated the real-world deployment and implementation of a machine learning surgical case duration model assisting surgical schedulers, but does not test a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice comparative to another.
